description:
Found by the fz-kdt.127 research (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1, r2/report.md
(b) and surprise 4). AnyValue::as_float (src/ir_interp/value.rs:91-97)
returns Some(v as f64) for Int(v); extern_call.rs:65-73 marshal_arg(F64)
uses it, and binop.rs:14-24 has the same lenience. When a value is routed
into a body compiled for a float lane (samelambda3's int closure inside
twice[closure[L](float)] -> fz_op_add_if with [I64, F64] given [Int(1),
Int(10)]), the interp silently converts and prints 11.0 / 12.0. Native at
the same seam refuses at compile time (lower_closure_capture) or would
read raw bits.

The lenience hides a whole class of misroutes on the door that is supposed
to be the oracle. Make the marshal strict (a tagged Int reaching an F64
lane is a fault with the executable and lane named), and re-run the
corpus on interp to find what was silently coerced. Red-first witness:
sl3.fz at HEAD must FAULT on interp instead of printing 12.0 (until
fz-kdt.127 lands, after which it prints 12). Check FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_
SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP: it was silent on sl3 because no test was asked; the
strict marshal is the complementary tripwire at the lane.
title: Interp accepts an Int under an F64 extern marshal: every int-into-float-lane misroute prints a plausible number instead of faulting
